title: Delta-hash onboarding and dynamic pin policy for community models
creator: Aisha Rodriguez
description:
Goal: Add a delta-hash-based detection step to model ingestion and implement a dynamic pinning policy that decides whether to automatically pin a newly onboarded community model variant or defer pinning until performance signatures are validated. This reduces noisy pins, prevents regressions from bad community uploads, and improves catalog hygiene without slowing down onboarding for high-confidence artifacts.

Context: We ingest many community models with small diffs (tokenizer-only updates, metadata-only pushes, or identical weights repackaged). Current workflow pins variants by naive heuristics (timestamp + origin) which creates too many 'pinned-but-unverified' models in the catalog. We also publish performance profiles immediately which can be misleading if the artifact was incorrectly packaged.

Scope and deliverables:
- Implement a delta-hash step in the ingest pipeline that computes a compact delta signature between the incoming model manifest and the closest existing variant. The delta-hash should be tolerant to metadata-only changes and focus on weight/signature diffs.
- Extend the manifest schema with a new field "delta_hash" and an enumerated "pin_decision" metadata value (auto-pin | hold-for-eval | manual-review).
- Build a dynamic pinning service that consumes delta_hash + quick synthetic perf signals to decide pin_decision. Rules: identical or near-identical (delta threshold) => auto-pin; small metadata-only changes => auto-pin but mark provenance; unknown/large-delta => hold-for-eval and run staged perf jobs.
- Integrate with the performance profile publishing pipeline: only publish full perf profiles for variants that are auto-pinned or that pass the staged perf-eval gate. For hold-for-eval variants, publish a minimal placeholder profile with a note linking to the active evaluation job.
- Add validation checks and a rollback path: if a later perf regression is detected (regression alerts), automatically unpin the variant and mark for manual review with linked regression artifacts.
- Update developer docs and onboarding playbook (Confluence link) + add Console visuals to show pin_decision state per variant.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ingest pipeline exposes delta_hash in manifests for 95% of onboarding events in staging.
- Dynamic pinning service correctly classifies 90%+ of trivial metadata-only updates as auto-pin in the test corpus.
- End-to-end test: a synthetic model with weight mutation beyond threshold gets classified hold-for-eval and does not appear in the public catalog until a perf-eval job completes.
- No increase in median onboarding latency > 250ms for auto-pin happy-path.
- Documentation updated with examples and playbook steps; Console shows new pin_decision states and links to perf-eval jobs.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Design: finalize delta-hash algorithm, schema change, and gate thresholds. Produce a short spec and API contract. Owner: Liam. (Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Delta+Hash+Spec)
2) Ingest pipeline change: compute delta_hash in the ingestion lambda and annotate staging manifests. Add unit tests. Owner: Platform ingestion team.
3) Pinning service: new microservice that evaluates delta + quick synthetic runs (10-shot token generation budget) to emit pin_decision. Expose an idempotent API for manifest enrichment. Owner: Catalog team.
4) Perf-eval integration: wire hold-for-eval to the perf pipeline (job queue + ephemeral runners). Add minimal placeholder profile flow. Owner: Evaluations team.
5) Console + docs: surface pin_decision and provide actions (force pin, request manual review). Owner: Console and Docs teams.
6) Rollout: feature-flagged in staging, run canary on 5% ingest events, monitor false-positive/negative rates, iterate thresholds.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Delta-hash design: compute at object-weight chunk level vs whole artifact hash. Chunking is more accurate but more CPU/time. We'll prototype both and pick based on cost/accuracy.
- Quick synthetic perf runs are noisy; threshold tuning will require several days of telemetry. We will start conservative to avoid false auto-pins.
- Risk of increasing ingest latency. We'll make delta-hash async for large artifacts and rely on prior fingerprints when available.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for delta-hash computation, deterministic results over canonical artifacts.
- Integration tests: ingest->pinning->manifest enrichment->perf pipeline mock.
- Canary: run on 5% of staging then 1% in prod for first week. Create monitoring dashboard for pin_decision distribution, onboarding latency, and post-pin regression alerts.

Rollback and incident response:
- If we see a spike in regressions originating from auto-pinned variants, immediately toggle the feature flag to opt-out auto-pin and revert to manual pin queue.
- Have a daily automated job for the first 7 days that validates new pins against a small benchmark suite; failures unpin and create an auto-investigation ticket.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Delta+Hash+Spec
- Draft PR for ingest changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821
- Perf pipeline spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Perf+Eval+Gate
- Mock dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/pin-decision-canary

Notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on the metadata/pinning decision surface and integration with the perf publishing flow. Lower-level kernel/runtime optimizations for faster synthetic runs are tracked in separate engineering tickets (see dependencies).
